findings.title: SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK's catalogued rule omits RULE.CIT.DOI, which RULES.toml and the scan's own comment attribute to it
findings.description: catalog/scans.toml's single-valued rule column for SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK names only RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE. But policy/RULES.toml independently records RULE.CIT.DOI's check as this same scan id, and the scan's own file-header comment agrees it enforces both rules — confirmed by reading the implementation, which both cross-checks DOIs against the canonical reference list (RULE.CIT.DOI's concern) and flags a full reference in a docstring's running prose (RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE's concern). SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE and SCAN.DEAD_REF also carry two-rule header comments, but for those RULES.toml's check registry agrees with the single-rule catalogue attribution; only here does RULES.toml name the scan as a rule's check that scans.toml's own row omits.
findings.resolution_hint: Widen catalog/scans.toml's rule column to a list and record both RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE and RULE.CIT.DOI for SCAN.DOI_CROSSCHECK, so scans.toml and RULES.toml agree on which rules the scan is catalogued as enforcing.
